references.text: Moses gathered the children of Israel to give them the Lord's commands, just as he did after receiving the tablets of the law on Mount Sinai.
The Lord gave Moses instructions that were to be communicated to the congregation of Israel, which is repeated here in chapter 35.
Moses gathered the entire congregation at the entrance of the tent of meeting, a parallel to how he gathered the people to give them the Lord's commands.
Moses conveyed the commands and regulations that the Lord had ordered him to teach the people.
The Lord commanded Moses to teach the people commands and regulations that they were to keep.
Detailed instructions about the tabernacle which Moses now conveys to the people after coming down from the mountain.
Moses was faithful in all God's house and faithfully conveyed everything God commanded him.
Both verses mark a formal transfer of God's commands from Moses to the leadership using the same authoritative introductory formula.
A direct parallel in both situation (Moses speaking to the congregation) and wording, emphasizing that holy acts must always begin with God's explicit command.
Direct narrative follow-up: 39:42 confirms that the work was done exactly as commanded in 35:1.
The use of the same authoritative introductory formula emphasizes that both ceremonial laws and practical service require direct commands from God.
Both verses link God's specific command directly to the manifestation of the Lord's presence (the glory) through obedience.
